children: Workday

shares jumped about 7% after the enterprise-software company topped Wall Street's quarterly expectations and showed that artificial intelligence is becoming a meaningful source of new business. The standout figure for investors was not simply the earnings beat: AI generated more than
25% of Workday's new annual contract value
, offering an early sign that its agent strategy could strengthen subscription growth.

Workday sells cloud-based financial management software to businesses, generating most of its revenue through recurring subscriptions. That makes subscription growth and contracted backlog especially important indicators of future revenue momentum.
Second-quarter adjusted earnings reached
$2.75 per share
, ahead of the $2.61 analysts expected. Revenue rose
12.8% to $2.65 billion
, narrowly beating the $2.64 billion consensus estimate. Subscription revenue increased
13.9% to $2.47 billion
, above management's $2.455 billion guidance.
Forward indicators were also constructive. Workday's 12-month subscription backlog climbed
14.2% to $9.03 billion
, while total subscription backlog increased 8% to
$27.40 billion

We had a strong Q2, with AI driving more than 25% of our new annual contract value and more than 5,500 customers now using at least one of our organic agents, CEO Aneel Bhusri said. CFO Zane Rowe said the quarter reflected continued momentum across our platform, with AI emerging as a strategic driver of customer expansion.
Workday now expects current-quarter subscription revenue of
$2.515 billion
, up 12%, with a 30% adjusted operating margin. Fiscal 2027 subscription revenue is projected at
$9.94 billion to $9.95 billion
, slightly tightening and raising the low end of its previous forecast.
Investor takeaway
The key question is whether AI can move from an encouraging contract-growth contributor into a durable accelerator of Workday's overall subscription business.
Investors should watch
new annual contract value, subscription backlog growth and operating margins
. The 25% AI contribution to new ACV suggests Workday is already monetizing its agent products rather than simply promising future revenue.
Still, Wall Street appears relatively cautious after the rally. Workday carries a
Moderate Buy
consensus among 29 analysts, with 14 Buy, 13 Hold and two Sell ratings. The average
$207.67 price target implied only about 2% upside
at the time of the source report.

Faster backlog growth and continued AI-driven customer expansion could force estimates higher. If subscription growth settles closer to the low-teens pace despite rising AI adoption, however, investors may question how much incremental growth the new products are actually generating.

title: Workday Stock Surges After Major AI Growth Signal
